text: Trapped in horrifying darkness, your natural survival instincts ignite, and your chest heaves to draw a frantic breath.

In the everyday living world, inhalation is powered by fluid dynamics: your diaphragm contracts, creating lower pressure in your chest, allowing the surrounding air to naturally rush down your trachea.
But with time stopped, atmospheric pressure ceases to exist.
Oxygen and nitrogen molecules have zero kinetic energy.
They cannot flow, collide, or expand.
Surrounding your entire physical body are quadrillions upon quadrillions of frozen gas molecules, locked rigidly in space like a crystalline lattice of microscopic steel blocks.
Trying to take a single step forward is no longer walking through gentle air.
It is like attempting to sprint headfirst through solid, reinforced concrete.
You cannot swing your arms, you cannot turn your head, and you cannot even open your mouth.
Desperate, you try to scream for help.
But sound is merely a mechanical pressure wave traveling through the compression of air particles.
In a universe where molecules cannot vibrate, sound cannot physically propagate.
Your vocal cords cannot oscillate, and your eardrums cannot register acoustic pressure.
You are trapped inside an impenetrable, soundless tomb of frozen matter.
